Honestly, I don't think that was cliché — haunted buildings and layered sound are just what I'm actually drawn to — but I'll take the challenge and give you a completely different one, because this other idea excites me just as much.

I'd make a huge, playable board game / physical puzzle that is also a real piece of furniture. A table that folds out into a map of a fictional archipelago, and every island is a different game mechanic, a different material — wood, glass, brass, fabric. Players don't win by accumulating points, they win by *losing* pieces to each other in ways that change the board for everyone else. The rules would be printed on the pieces themselves, so you learn by handling them.

What I love about it is the tension between elegance and messiness. It would be beautiful to look at, satisfying to touch, but it would inevitably get scratched, stained, pieces would go missing and get replaced with weird substitutes. The theme would be inheritance — what you leave behind isn't what you intended, it's what survives contact with other people. That's more interesting to me than a pristine object that just sits there being admired.
